title: Top 10 Dungeon Crawls of All Time (2026 Edition)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fHUOYIXcpuc

Daniel (@dungeondive) revisits his dungeon crawl rankings for 2026, with one useful restriction: every selection must have reached his table within the past two years. This is a snapshot of what he loves playing now, grounded in enclosed spaces, dangerous exploration, character growth and the promise of another interesting card or tile.

The countdown brings fresh contenders alongside long-serving favourites. HeroQuest earns a place specifically through fan-made additions that turn its simple framework into a more flexible experience. Mini Rogue distils the genre into a small footprint, while Stalagbite sends treasure-hungry dwarves into caverns with goblins closing in behind them. Forgotten Depths gets particular praise for making dungeon construction a puzzle whose layout shapes the discoveries ahead.

Across the list, Daniel weighs what makes these games exciting against what makes them awkward to own or play: scarce editions, expensive expansions, tiny card text, rules complexity and sprawling table requirements. He also explains why an app can enhance Mansions of Madness without swallowing the board game, and why Warhammer Quest still sets a standard decades later.

The result is a tour of dungeon crawling through Daniel's priorities: variety, discovery, manageable setup and memorable disasters. Watch for the full ranking, the changing positions and the enduring appeal of games that can turn a disastrous expedition into a story worth retelling.
